topic: Career angle: employers want AI builders, not just prompters (Workday report)
post:
"Good at prompting" is no longer enough for your resume. 📉
Employers now want people who can BUILD with AI.

That's the signal from Workday's new Global Workforce Report, based on job postings from 550+ employers plus a survey of 6,001 workers and leaders.

What it found:

📉 Demand for basic AI skills like simple prompting peaked in January, then fell 25%
📈 Demand for building AI tools, automating workflows and AI engineering rose 51% (Sept 2025 to July 2026)
🤝 40% of leaders expect AI to get more out of current staff. Only 28% expect it to cut headcount.

My read 👇
Prompting is becoming like typing: everyone is expected to know it, so it no longer stands out.
The edge is moving to people who turn AI into a working process for their team.

Why it matters:
AI is rewriting jobs more than replacing them. The people who redesign their own work will write the new job descriptions.

Practical takeaway:
This week, pick ONE repetitive task you do every week and automate part of it with an AI tool. Then write down the before-and-after. That's a resume line. 📝

What's one task you'd automate first? 👇

Follow for daily AI news you can actually use.
